name: Toofan
summary: Amitabh Bachchan's bow-and-arrow-wielding Hanuman devotee from the 1989 Hindi film Toofan, directed by Ketan Desai. His twin brother is a street magician.
origin: Toofan is the superpowered half of a pair of twins played by Amitabh Bachchan in the 1989 Hindi film. The hero is a devotee of Hanuman who fights with a bow and arrow, while his brother Shyam is a timid magician who wants to complete an escape act that cost the life of the street magician who raised him. Pran plays Inspector Hanuman Prasad Singh, credited as the twins' father. Toofan was written by Salim Khan and K. K. Shukla.
powers: Superhuman strength attributed to a divine blessing
Magical bow and arrow, a gift of Hanuman's blessing in the film
Deadly aim, including a rope-like arrow shot to grab a helicopter

storyline.title: Twin brothers
storyline.beat: Two brothers grow up apart: one with superpowers and a devotion to Hanuman, the other a gentle magician raised by a street magician.

storyline.title: A blessing and a bow
storyline.beat: In the film, the hero receives a magical bow and arrow through the blessing of Hanuman and sets out against the criminals who wronged his family.

storyline.title: The magician's trick
storyline.beat: Shyam wants to perform the escape act that cost the magician who raised him his life, which ties the magic plot to the hero plot.

storyline.title: The helicopter chase
storyline.beat: The climax has the hero use his arrow to hitch himself to a helicopter carrying the villain.

gossip.text: Republic says Manmohan Desai and his son Ketan discussed casting Rishi Kapoor, but Ketan judged the part too small for his star status, so Farooq Sheikh was signed instead.

gossip.truth: Wikipedia calls it an average grosser after a very strong opening, while Republic's trivia list calls it a failure, so sources differ.

gossip.text: Some reports at the time suggested children were enjoying the superhero film after its full-house opening in Mumbai.
Republic notes that Amrita Singh's character in Toofan has no name, while Wikipedia's cast list calls her only 'Pickpocketer'.

quiz.q: Who plays both Toofan and his twin Shyam?
quiz.why: Amitabh Bachchan has the double role.

quiz.q: What is Shyam's job in the film?

quiz.why: He is a devotee of Hanuman.

quiz.q: What arrives with Toofan every time he appears?
quiz.why: A swirling dust storm announces his arrival on horseback every time.
His cape is black and saffron.

theme.tagline: Storm-wind, saffron and one very long arrow.

timeline.title: Toofan released
timeline.note: Ketan Desai directs Amitabh Bachchan in a double role; the opening is strong, with full houses in Mumbai.

timeline.title: Opens beside Nigahen
timeline.note: Toofan and the equally awaited Nigahen open in cinemas on the same day, according to Republic's trivia list.

timeline.title: Elaan-E-Jung arrives
timeline.note: Toofan falls in its second week when Elaan-E-Jung opens, with Dharmendra and Jaya Prada.

timeline.title: An average grosser
timeline.note: Wikipedia lists a Rs 4 crore budget against a Rs 8 crore gross, and calls it an average result.

timeline.title: Desai's last Bachchan film recalled
timeline.note: Producer Manmohan Desai dies on 1 March 1994; Toofan was his last film with Bachchan.

facts.text: The finale has Toofan fire his arrow so that it hitches him to a helicopter carrying his father's killer. Scroll recounts it as the finale of the film.
Toofan rides into trouble on horseback, and a swirling dust storm always announces his arrival, according to Scroll's description of the film.
For the storm scenes, director Ketan Desai used nine storm fans and also hired 200 local people to climb trees and shake them by hand.
'Aaya Toofan' was Kishore Kumar's last song for an Amitabh Bachchan film before his death, yet his name is missing from the end credits even though the other singers are credited.
'Haa Bhai Haa Mai Hu Jawaan' borrows from the Iranian hit 'Havar Havar' by Kourosh Yaghmaei. Wikipedia says that tune also inspired songs in the films Billoo Badshah and Aag Ka Gola.
'Don't Worry Be Happy' in Toofan takes its inspiration from Bobby McFerrin's song of the same name. Manhar Udhas and Bachchan himself sing it, and Jagdeep and Sonu Walia make guest appearances.
Toofan was the last film Amitabh Bachchan made with producer Manmohan Desai, after about 12 years of working together, according to Republic's trivia list.
Republic calls it a little-known detail that the opening line of the song 'Jaadugar Ka Jaadu' plays on Bachchan's own name, with a pun on the Hindi word for children.
Pran plays Inspector Hanuman Prasad Singh, the twins' father, a name that matches the god his son worships. Republic says it is the only film in which Pran made a special appearance.
Toofan was launched in 1987 but held up by production problems. Wikipedia says reshoots followed after Gangaa Jamunaa Saraswati (1988), also with Bachchan and Meenakshi Seshadri, flopped.
Gangaa Jamunaa Saraswati was directed by Manmohan Desai himself. It opened on 23 December 1988 to excellent collections, then sank, and India Today called it a disaster by January 1989.
Scroll says Toofan's black and saffron cape marks him out as a divine soul, a visual cue for the hero's holy backing.
Republic says the makers gave Goga Kapoor the chance to play the film's leading villain; Wikipedia lists him as the bandit chief Daku Shaitan Singh.
Wikipedia's infobox lists Toofan at 176 minutes, with a budget of Rs 4 crore and a gross of Rs 8 crore, double its cost, yet the film is still called an average grosser.
Scroll contrasts Bachchan's caped run: in Shahenshah his hero has no magic, while Toofan's weapon is a magical bow and arrow gained through Hanuman's direct blessing.
The soundtrack is by Anu Malik with lyrics by Indeevar. Toofan is also the only film in which Suresh Wadkar sang for Amitabh Bachchan, Wikipedia notes.
Toofan had a very strong opening, but it crashed in its second week when Elaan-E-Jung, starring Dharmendra and Jaya Prada, arrived in cinemas.
Producer Manmohan Desai is called a pioneer of masala films whose plots often split families and reunite them, a pattern that fits Toofan's twins raised apart.
In the Valmiki Ramayana, as told on Wikipedia, the child Hanuman leaps for the sun, mistaking it for fruit, and the gods then grant him boons of strength. Toofan's hero follows this god.
Salim Khan wrote Toofan in 1989, the same year his son Salman Khan's film Maine Pyar Kiya reached cinemas, Republic's trivia list says.

kidSummary: Toofan is a 1989 Hindi film in which Amitabh Bachchan plays twin brothers. One is a gentle street magician. The other is super strong, rides a horse in a swirl of dust, and, in the film, gets a magical bow through the blessing of Hanuman. The finale is a daring helicopter chase.
